title: Cells at Work!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Inside an adult human body pictured as a city, anthropomorphized cells each do their jobs. A rookie red blood cell, AE3803, who often gets lost on deliveries, keeps running into a gentle but ruthless white blood cell, U-1146, who kills invading germs. Each chapter turns an infection, injury or allergy into an action-comedy with short explanations of real biology.
life_message: Every worker, however small, matters when each does its job for the good of the whole body.

content.note: Immune cells slaughter pathogens with lots of blood, played for comedy-action (Wikipedia; AniList Gore; MU Violence).
Infections and a cancer storyline (MU Cancer; Wikipedia).

Feelings of inferiority overcome by a cell (Wikipedia).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Cells do jobs by rules; rivalries are comic (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Each cell keeps strictly to its assigned role (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty is to the whole body, not to kin (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Command structure of helper and killer T cells (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Real biology taught; praised for accuracy (Wikipedia).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Constant fight to keep the body alive (AniList Survival).

folkways.japan: The diligent, uniformed workers who each keep to their role mirror Japanese workplace and group-harmony ideals.

delivery.evidence: Facts given through explanatory text and pathogens describing themselves like supervillains (Wikipedia, Encyclopedia of Science Fiction).

personified.ideology: A world where cells need not kill each other, even at the body's risk
Cell types should keep to their own kind

delivery.note: The lesson is mostly science, stated openly; the moral of duty to the whole is carried by the setup.

winners_losers: The immune system and the body's order win; invading pathogens and rogue cells lose; duty to the whole gets sympathy.
